title: Where a cool-water seaweed that needs nutrients could grow
query: A canopy-forming seaweed is assumed to need a surface nitrate concentration above 1 mmol/m3 in winter and a mean sea surface temperature of the warmest month below 19 C. Using the supplied GLORYS12 daily near-surface temperature and CMEMS biogeochemical reanalysis monthly nitrate for 1993-2020 in the western Tasman Sea off south-eastern Australia (46-26 S, 147-162 E), determine where both conditions were met in each year, how the suitable area and its northern limit changed over the record, which of the two conditions limits it where, and how sensitive the answer is to the two thresholds and to combining a daily product with a monthly one. The two products come from different model systems; account for that.

region.name: Tasman Sea and East Australian Current
